summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and essential tremor was admitted for IV hydration and a CT angiogram following an ultrasound that suggested hepatic artery stenosis. She was asymptomatic and had undergone a liver biopsy earlier in the day for evaluation of rising liver enzymes. The CT scan ruled out hepatic artery stenosis but revealed a new small thrombosis in a subsegmental branch of the right posterior portal vein, which will be monitored outpatient. Her home medications were continued with lisinopril held for the scan and to be restarted post-discharge. She experienced a mild hypoglycemic episode managed with oral glucose and will continue her insulin regimen. Concerns about medication management and home safety prompted a referral to Elder Affairs. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up on biopsy results, the portal vein thrombus, and osteopenia management.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of liver
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Other disorders of bone and cartilage
Essential and other specified forms of tremor
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Need for prophylactic vaccination and inoculation against influenza
